method: Three serial cohorts: native initial with fresh Torch, CUDA TIRx subgroup, native recheck.
The captured BR1 Tile IR, typed inputs, FP64 references and per-element bounds are identical. Only manifest.lowering differs; only logical IR analysis wall time is ignored.
fast_math=true is explicit on both native routes; their documented elementwise math implementations differ. This is not a claim of identical arithmetic instructions.
All 100 actual graph nodes per native result are checked against the loaded function, full launch geometry and final typed argument pointers; subgroup uses the emitted argument permutation.
Original numerical/finite/guard/readonly receipts and full saved-output checks are required independently of speed.
Driver registers/shared/local/max-threads are compiled attributes, not measured occupancy, traffic or causes of performance.
All seven raw samples and all negative results are retained; smaller candidate/control ratios are better. No fitting, trimming or improvement gate.
Torch uses compiled functional output allocation while native routes preallocate output. The shared timing protocol does not erase that contract difference.
No earlier smoke, row-regroup or math-mode cohort supplies a timing denominator.
telemetry_scope: Whole-stage telemetry includes compilation, upload, warmup and measurement; no causal attribution.
